symbols.name: qK
symbols.def: \(q_{P^{(n)},K}(u)\) is the smallest center in \(C_{P^{(n)},K}\) attaining \(\min_{c\in C_{P^{(n)},K}}|u-c|\).

symbols.name: ZP
symbols.def: \((Z_{P^{(n)},K}:1\le K<K_n)\) is centered Gaussian with covariance \(R_{P^{(n)}}\).

symbols.name: hatGK
symbols.def: \(\widehat G_K=\widehat\rho(K+1)-\widehat\rho(K)\), where every \(\widehat W_K\) is a cross-fitted corrected loss minimized over \(\mathcal C_K\), every inverse propensity uses \(\widehat e^{\mathrm{cl}}\), \(\widehat\rho(K)=1-\widehat W_K/\widehat W_1\), and every nonunique empirical minimizer is resolved by the deterministic measurable rule selecting the lexicographically smallest ordered codebook.

symbols.name: tildepsiK
symbols.def: \(\widetilde\psi_{i,K}\) is the uncentered cross-fitted plug-in value for \(\Delta\phi_{P^{(n)},K}(O_{n,i})\), evaluated with the nuisance fits and deterministic empirical codebook selectors trained outside the fold containing unit \(i\), and with \(\widehat e^{\mathrm{cl}}\) in every inverse weight.

symbols.name: hatsigmaK
symbols.def: \(\widehat\sigma_K^2=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n(\widehat{\Delta\phi}_{i,K})^2\) and \(\widehat\sigma_K=\{\widehat\sigma_K^2\}^{1/2}\) is the nonnegative square root.

symbols.name: xi
symbols.def: Conditionally on the data, \(\xi_1,\ldots,\xi_n\stackrel{\mathrm{iid}}{\sim}N(0,1)\) and are independent of the data.

symbols.name: qalpha
symbols.def: Let \(T_n^{\#}=\max_{1\le K<K_n:\widehat\sigma_K>0}|n^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^n\xi_i\widehat{\Delta\phi}_{i,K}/\widehat\sigma_K|\), with the maximum over the empty set defined as zero. Then \(q_{n,1-\alpha}^{\#}=\inf\{t\in\mathbb R:P(T_n^{\#}\le t\mid O_{n,1},\ldots,O_{n,n})\ge1-\alpha\}\).

symbols.name: IK
symbols.def: If \(\widehat\sigma_K>0\), then \(I_{n,K}=[\widehat G_K-q_{n,1-\alpha}^{\#}\widehat\sigma_K/\sqrt n,\widehat G_K+q_{n,1-\alpha}^{\#}\widehat\sigma_K/\sqrt n]\); if \(\widehat\sigma_K=0\), set \(I_{n,K}=\mathbb R\).

symbols.name: Bsharp
symbols.def: \(B_n^{\#}=\prod_{1\le K<K_n}I_{n,K}\) is the single data-measurable band produced by the corrected estimator and multiplier quantile.

symbols.name: PU
symbols.def:
Under \(P_{U,
u_n}^{(n)}\), \(X=U\), \(A\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\) independently of \(U\), \(Y(1)=U-1/2+
u_n\varepsilon_1\), and \(Y(0)=1/2-U+
u_n\varepsilon_0\), with independent Rademacher marks \(\varepsilon_0,\varepsilon_1\).

symbols.name: Bp
symbols.def: \(B_1(t)=t-1/2\) and \(B_2(t)=t^2-t+1/6\) for \(t\in[0,1)\), extended with period one.

symbols.name: cfano
symbols.def: \(c_{\mathrm F}>0\) is fixed and sufficiently small.

symbols.name: Ptilt
symbols.def:
For \(j\in J_n\), \[ rac{dP_j^{(n)}}{dP_{U,
u_n}^{(n)}}(o)= rac{\exp\{\delta_n s_{n,j}(o)\}}{\mathbb E_{P_{U,
u_n}^{(n)}}[\exp\{\delta_n s_{n,j}(O)\}]},\] together with the base law \(P_0^{(n)}=P_{U,
u_n}^{(n)}\).

symbols.name: Un
symbols.def: \(\mathcal U_n=\{P_0^{(n)}\}\cup\{P_j^{(n)}:j\in J_n\}\), with the laws supplied by \(Ptilt\).

symbols.name: Vband
symbols.def: \(V_n\sim\operatorname{Unif}[0,1]\) is independent of the sample under every row law; a procedure that does not randomize ignores this argument.

symbols.name: bandLower
symbols.def: \(L_{n,K}=L_{n,K}(O_{n,1},\ldots,O_{n,n},V_n)\) is measurable and does not depend on \(P^{(n)}\).

symbols.name: bandUpper
symbols.def: \(U_{n,K}=U_{n,K}(O_{n,1},\ldots,O_{n,n},V_n)\) is measurable, does not depend on \(P^{(n)}\), and satisfies \(L_{n,K}\le U_{n,K}\).

symbols.name: Bband
symbols.def: \(B_n(O_{n,1},\ldots,O_{n,n},V_n)=\prod_{1\le K<K_n}[L_{n,K},U_{n,K}]\) is one common \(P^{(n)}\)-independent measurable map.

symbols.name: bandHalf
symbols.def: \(h_{n,K}=(U_{n,K}-L_{n,K})/2\), with \(h_{n,K}=+\infty\) when an endpoint is infinite.

symbols.name: HonestBand
symbols.type: uniform-honesty predicate over the local experiment
symbols.def: \(\operatorname{Honest}_{\alpha}(B_n,\mathcal U_n)\) holds when there exists a deterministic sequence \(\eta_n\downarrow0\) such that \[\inf_{P^{(n)}\in\mathcal U_n}\mathbb P_{P^{(n)}}^n\{G_{P^{(n)}}(K)\in[L_{n,K},U_{n,K}]\text{ for every }1\le K<K_n\}\ge1-\alpha-\eta_n.\] The probability integrates the declared auxiliary randomization.

assumptions.condition: \(\epsilon\le e_{P^{(n)}}(X)\le1-\epsilon\) almost surely for a fixed \(\epsilon\in(0,1/2)\).

novel.justification: The normalization fixes a common interpretable scale for customer-level causal contrasts and is satisfied after rescaling any application with a known bounded contrast range, including binary outcomes and the uniform randomized-trial witness.

assumptions.condition: For every \(1\le K\le K_n\), \(C_{P^{(n)},K}\) is a singleton \((c_{P^{(n)},K,1},\ldots,c_{P^{(n)},K,K})\) satisfying \(0<c_{P^{(n)},K,1}<\cdots<c_{P^{(n)},K,K}<1\).

novel.justification: Unique interior population segmentations are stable for scalar feature laws with densities bounded above and below near the uniform law; the condition rules out scientifically ambiguous tied segmentations while allowing cell widths and curvature to deteriorate with resolution.

assumptions.condition: For every \(K\le K_n\) and every ordered codebook \(C\in\mathcal C_K\) with \(\min_{\pi}\|C-\pi C_{P^{(n)},K}\|_2\le\kappa_{P^{(n)},K}\), its excess distortion is at least \(\lambda_{P^{(n)},K}\min_{\pi}\|C-\pi C_{P^{(n)},K}\|_2^2\).

novel.justification: A local quadratic-growth modulus is the nonsmooth formulation of optimizer stability needed for increasing resolution; it holds for densities bounded away from zero around the uniform law and does not presume twice differentiability of the distortion.

assumptions.condition: For every \(K\le K_n\) and \(0<t\le\kappa_{P^{(n)},K}\), \(P^{(n)}[\operatorname{dist}\{b_{P^{(n)}}(X),\mathcal B_{P^{(n)},K}\}\le t s_{P^{(n)},K}]\le M_{P^{(n)},K}t^{\alpha_{P^{(n)},K}}\).

novel.justification: This resolution-indexed version of the quantization margin condition retains the shrinking cell radius and is satisfied uniformly by scalar densities bounded near the uniform density; Levrard's fixed-resolution margin condition is its geometric antecedent.

assumptions.condition: The primitive functions \(e_{P^{(n)}},\mu_{0,P^{(n)}},\mu_{1,P^{(n)}}\) admit cross-fitted estimators whose maximum \(L_2(P_X^{(n)})\) error, with uniform error for the two outcome regressions, is \(O_{P^{(n)}}(r_n)\) uniformly over the row class.

novel.justification: The lower bound isolates a nonvanishing causal-heterogeneity regime in which the ratio profile is uniformly defined; it is satisfied by the uniform witness, for which \(W(1)=1/12\), and excludes drift to a homogeneous-effect law.

Positive adjacent-score variance is the minimal coordinatewise condition for studentizing resolution gains; the exact witness calculation verifies it while allowing the raw variances to shrink at resolution-dependent rates.

definitions.name: triangular causal-quantizer class
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal P_n^{\mathrm{CQ}}=\{P^{(n)}:P^{(n)}\text{ satisfies ass:consistency, ass:exchangeability, ass:overlap, ass:bounded-feature, ass:unique-interior-codebooks, ass:quadratic-growth, ass:growing-margin, ass:nuisance-estimability, ass:resolution-denominator, and ass:score-nondegeneracy for row }n\}\).

definitions.name: corrected growing-resolution profile
definitions.construction: On each validation fold, clip the fitted propensity to \([\epsilon/2,1-\epsilon/2]\), insert it and the fitted outcome regressions into the corrected loss induced by \(\phi_{W,P^{(n)},K}\), minimize the empirical corrected loss over \(\mathcal C_K\) for every \(1\le K\le K_n\), select the lexicographically smallest ordered minimizer, and form \(\widehat G_K\), the raw foldwise values \(\widetilde\psi_{i,K}\), their mean \(\overline\psi_K\), the centered values \(\widehat{\Delta\phi}_{i,K}\), and the nonnegative \(\widehat\sigma_K\) as declared in the symbol table.

definitions.name: common measurable rectangular band
definitions.construction: Fix one sequence of \(P^{(n)}\)-independent measurable maps \(B_n=\prod_{1\le K<K_n}[L_{n,K},U_{n,K}]\) with \(L_{n,K}\le U_{n,K}\), coordinate half-widths \(h_{n,K}=(U_{n,K}-L_{n,K})/2\), and only the declared independent \(V_n\) as optional auxiliary randomization. Uniform honesty over \(\mathcal U_n\) means \(\operatorname{Honest}_{\alpha}(B_n,\mathcal U_n)\) as declared in the symbol table.

definitions.name: covariance-aware multiplier band
definitions.construction: Compute \(q_{n,1-\alpha}^{\#}\) as the conditional quantile infimum of the joint multiplier maximum over exactly the coordinates with \(\widehat\sigma_K>0\), retaining the empirical cross-resolution covariance, and report \(\{I_{n,K}:1\le K<K_n\}\), with \(I_{n,K}=\mathbb R\) when \(\widehat\sigma_K=0\). This is a single common measurable rectangular-band procedure and uses neither oracle \(P^{(n)}\)-indexed endpoints nor independent-coordinate calibration.

definitions.name: multi-resolution Fano family
definitions.construction: Use the base law and all one-hot score tilts \(\{P_j^{(n)}:j\in J_n\}\) in the explicit construction of \(Ptilt\), with amplitude \(\delta_n\) and the full observed-data likelihood normalized separately for each resolution.

definitions.name: warped Bernoulli-score handle
definitions.construction: Start from the probability-integral transform of the causal-feature law, expand optimized residual and loss contrasts in the transported periodic Bernoulli basis, and orthogonalize the resulting score directions against the nuisance tangent space to target the observational cross-resolution kernel.

statements.statement:
For every row \(n\), every \(0\le
u_n\le1/4\), and every \(K\le K_n\), the law \(P_{U,
u_n}^{(n)}\) satisfies the causal, support, unique-interior-codebook, local quadratic-growth, growing-margin, denominator, and score-nondegeneracy conditions of \(\mathcal P_n^{\mathrm{CQ}}\). Its unique centers are \(c_{K,j}=(2j-1)/(2K)\), its boundaries are \(j/K\), and \(W_{P_{U,
u_n}^{(n)}}(K)=1/(12K^2)\).
statements.justification: This establishes a nonempty bounded causal experiment in which every geometric and inferential quantity is explicit.
statements.gap: Pollard1982Central and Levrard2015 analyze observed fixed-resolution quantizers, while KimKimKennedy2026 does not give a growing-resolution causal witness.
statements.consumer: MineThatData analysts obtain a calibrated benchmark for how many customer-effect segments can be distinguished under randomized-treatment noise.

statements.statement:
Under \(P_{U,
u_n}^{(n)}\), the complete adjacent-score covariance is \[\Sigma_{P_{U,
u_n}^{(n)}}(K,L)=144H_2(K,L)+576
u_n^2H_1(K,L).\] In particular, \(\sigma_{P_{U,
u_n}^{(n)},K}^2=V_K^{(0)}+
u_n^2A_K\). The arithmetic kernel implies \[\sup_{\substack{K
e L\,;\ K,L\ge8}}R_{P_{U,
u_n}^{(n)}}(K,L)\le0.28,\qquad d_{P_{U,
u_n}^{(n)}}(K,L)\ge1.2,\] uniformly over \(
u_n\in[0,1/4]\). Thus \(J_n\) is a covariance-separated packing with \(|J_n|=(K_n-8)_+\), and universal constants \(0<c<C<\infty\) satisfy \[c\sqrt{\log(2+K_n)}\le w_n(P_{U,
u_n}^{(n)})\le C\sqrt{\log(2+K_n)}.\]
statements.justification: The full covariance, rather than the diagonal variance or coordinate count, determines the simultaneous resolution penalty.
statements.gap: KimKimKennedy2026 supplies fixed-resolution influence functions and ChernozhukovChetverikovKato2017 supplies generic Gaussian approximation, but neither computes this arithmetic covariance kernel or its diverging packing.
statements.consumer: The covariance formula lets a MineThatData analysis replace conservative independent-coordinate calibration by the actual joint resolution geometry.

statements.statement: Uniformly over \(P^{(n)}\in\mathcal P_n^{\mathrm{CQ}}\), \[\max_{1\le K<K_n}\frac{|\widehat G_K-G_{P^{(n)}}(K)-(P_{\mathrm{emp},n}-P^{(n)})\Delta\phi_{P^{(n)},K}|}{\sigma_{P^{(n)},K}}=O_{P^{(n)}}\!\left(\max_{K<K_n}\frac{R^G_{P^{(n)},K,n}}{\sigma_{P^{(n)},K}}\right),\] and the maximum coordinatewise \(L_2(P^{(n)})\) discrepancy between \(\widehat{\Delta\phi}_{i,K}/\sigma_{P^{(n)},K}\) and \(\Delta\phi_{P^{(n)},K}(O_{n,i})/\sigma_{P^{(n)},K}\) is \(O_{P^{(n)}}(\max_{K<K_n}S^G_{P^{(n)},K,n}/\sigma_{P^{(n)},K})\). On \(\mathcal U_n\), the same bounds have constants uniform over the law, and \(\sup_{P^{(n)}\in\mathcal U_n}\Xi_n(P^{(n)})\to0\) implies the derived relative-variance consistency \[\max_{1\le K<K_n}\left|\frac{\widehat\sigma_K}{\sigma_{P^{(n)},K}}-1\right|=o_{P^{(n)}}(1)\quad\text{uniformly over }P^{(n)}\in\mathcal U_n.\] Consequently, \(\min_{K<K_n}\widehat\sigma_K>0\) with probability tending to one uniformly on \(\mathcal U_n\), and the optimized-risk, nuisance, score-estimation, and variance-estimation effects on the studentized maximum are negligible on the intrinsic Gaussian-width scale.
statements.justification: This is the changed technical step that keeps codebook reoptimization and causal nuisance error below the intrinsic Gaussian critical scale.
statements.gap: Levrard2015, Section 3.1, Theorem 3.1 and Section 3.2, Proposition 3.1 on PDF pages 10--12, tracks fixed-resolution quantizer risk and minimax geometry, while LiuPages2020, Abstract page 1 and Introduction pages 3--4, studies convergence of optimal \(K\)-level quantizers and distortion performance for Wasserstein-convergent measure sequences, including empirical measures, with level-dependent bounds. The published Abstract of KimKimKennedy2026, lines 134--163, reports plug-in and bias-corrected root-\(n\) fixed-target inference. These antecedents do not provide uniform \(K\le K_n\) control at shrinking adjacent-score scales or causal nuisance correction.
statements.consumer: The remainder comparison diagnoses whether finer MineThatData segmentation is limited first by codebook fitting or causal nuisance learning.

statements.statement: If \(\delta_n\max_{j\in J_n}\|s_{n,j}\|_\infty\to0\), every law in def:fano-family is normalized, preserves the support of \(P_{U,\nu_n}^{(n)}\), satisfies overlap with constant \(\epsilon/2\), and belongs to one common neighborhood in \(\mathcal P_n^{\mathrm{CQ}}\). Uniformly in \(j\in J_n\), its causal feature, optimizer, local quadratic-growth modulus, and boundary-margin constants differ from those of the base law by \(O(\delta_n)\), \[\max_{1\le K<K_n}\left|\frac{\sigma_{P_j^{(n)},K}}{\sigma_{P_0^{(n)},K}}-1\right|=o(1),\qquad \sup_{K,L<K_n}|R_{P_j^{(n)}}(K,L)-R_{P_0^{(n)}}(K,L)|=o(1).\] Moreover, \[G_{P_j^{(n)}}(K)-G_{P_0^{(n)}}(K)=\delta_n\sigma_{P_0^{(n)},K}R_{P_0^{(n)}}(K,j)+O(\delta_n^2\sigma_{P_0^{(n)},K})\] uniformly over \(K<K_n\). There is a fixed \(a_0>0\) such that \[\min_{j\ne\ell\,;\ j,\ell\in J_n}\max_{K\in J_n}\frac{|G_{P_j^{(n)}}(K)-G_{P_\ell^{(n)}}(K)|}{\sigma_{P_0^{(n)},K}}\ge a_0\delta_n\] for all sufficiently large \(n\), and \(\operatorname{KL}\{(P_j^{(n)})^{\otimes n},(P_0^{(n)})^{\otimes n}\}\le Cn\delta_n^2\).
statements.justification: The lower bound is credible only if the whole multi-resolution family remains inside the same causal-quantizer class and moves distinguishable covariance directions.
statements.gap: Levrard2015, Section 3.2, Proposition 3.1 on PDF pages 11--12, uses a fixed-resolution Assouad lower-bound construction for excess distortion; this claim certifies a growing observed-data causal packing aligned with adjacent efficient scores and supplies the variance conversion needed for standardized band length.
statements.consumer: The result supplies the least-favorable benchmark needed to interpret failure of fine-grained MineThatData resolution reports as information-theoretic rather than algorithmic.

statements.statement: If \(\sup_{P^{(n)}\in\mathcal U_n}\Xi_n(P^{(n)})\to0\), the band in def:intrinsic-bootstrap-band satisfies \(\operatorname{Honest}_{\alpha}(B_n^{\#},\mathcal U_n)\). On the event \(\min_{K<K_n}\widehat\sigma_K>0\), whose probability tends to one uniformly over \(\mathcal U_n\), its simultaneous standardized half-width obeys \[\max_{1\le K<K_n}\frac{q_{n,1-\alpha}^{\#}\widehat\sigma_K}{\sigma_{P^{(n)},K}}=q_{n,1-\alpha}^{\#}\{1+o_{P^{(n)}}(1)\}\asymp_{P^{(n)}}w_n(P^{(n)}).\] Conversely, for every sequence of common \(P^{(n)}\)-independent measurable rectangular-band procedures in def:rectangular-band-procedure satisfying \(\operatorname{Honest}_{\alpha}(B_n,\mathcal U_n)\), there exist constants \(c_0,c_1>0\), depending at most on the fixed \(\alpha\) and the chosen Fano constant \(c_{\mathrm F}\) but independent of \(n\), \(K_n\), and \(\nu_n\), such that for all sufficiently large \(n\) with \(|J_n|\ge2\), some \(P^{(n)}\in\mathcal U_n\) satisfies \[\mathbb P_{P^{(n)}}^n\left\{\max_{K\in J_n}\frac{\sqrt n\,h_{n,K}}{\sigma_{P^{(n)},K}}\ge c_0\sqrt{\log|J_n|}\right\}\ge c_1.\] By thm:exact-covariance-packing and thm:fano-membership, the achievable and necessary radii over \(\mathcal U_n\) have the same intrinsic order \(w_n(P^{(n)})/\sqrt n\asymp\sqrt{\log K_n/n}\).
statements.justification: This is the publishable kernel: the covariance-aware upper band and the multi-resolution information bound meet at the same intrinsic width.
statements.gap: The published Abstract of KimKimKennedy2026, lines 134--163, gives fixed-target plug-in and bias-corrected root-\(n\) causal \(k\)-means inference. Levrard2015, Section 3.1, Theorem 3.1 and Section 3.2, Proposition 3.1 on PDF pages 10--12, gives fixed-resolution excess-distortion upper and minimax lower bounds. LiuPages2020, Abstract page 1 and Introduction pages 3--4, is a fixed- and level-by-level antecedent for optimal-quantizer convergence and distortion performance, with quantization-level-dependent bounds. The title page and Abstract of BelloniChernozhukovChetverikovWei2018 on page 3643 describe simultaneous regions for many orthogonal-score parameters, and ChernozhukovChetverikovKato2017, preprint Theorem 2.1 and multiplier-bootstrap Section 4, supplies Gaussian and bootstrap approximation for given high-dimensional sums. These verified results do not match an upper and lower simultaneous radius over \(\mathcal U_n\) based on joint adjacent efficient-score covariance, multiplier calibration, and a multi-resolution causal Fano lower bound.
statements.consumer: A MineThatData report gains an honest, rate-optimal rule for displaying the entire customer-segmentation resolution curve with its unavoidable joint uncertainty.

statements.justification: The reduction rejects a raw-gap heuristic and checks both the noiseless and noisy high-resolution regimes against the fixed-coordinate case.
statements.gap: KimKimKennedy2026 establishes fixed-target asymptotic normality but does not derive the adjacent standardized-gap phase transition.
statements.consumer: The phase transition tells MineThatData users when outcome noise, rather than geometric quantization error, determines the finest reportable segmentation.

statements.statement: Using def:heteroskedastic-extension-handle, characterize the weakest primitive conditions under which a nonuniform causal-feature law with heteroskedastic efficient residual admits an explicit cross-resolution semimetric, a diverging covariance-separated packing, and a corrected band whose upper radius and multi-resolution lower bound both equal its intrinsic Gaussian width. Determine when the width is \(\sqrt{\log K_n}\), \(\sqrt{\log\log K_n}\), or bounded.
statements.justification: The uniform arithmetic kernel is a sharp benchmark, but empirical causal-feature densities can induce qualitatively different dependence across resolutions.
statements.gap: The supplied-score approximation papers do not derive covariance geometry from an optimized causal target, and the causal clustering papers do not classify intrinsic simultaneous complexity.
statements.consumer: An answer would let observational heterogeneous-treatment-effect studies select the correct joint penalty from their estimated feature geometry rather than inherit the uniform benchmark.

sampling_model.design: Observational or randomized binary-treatment rows satisfying consistency, conditional exchangeability, and overlap; the exact lower-bound witness is a randomized trial.
sampling_model.units: For each row \(n\), \(O_{n,1},\ldots,O_{n,n}\) are independent draws from \(P^{(n)}\).
sampling_model.overlap: A fixed \(\epsilon\)-overlap condition is imposed, and fitted propensities are clipped by construction.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Cross-fitted propensity and outcome-regression learners attain the primitive rate \(r_n\); codebooks are reoptimized separately at every resolution.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The published Abstract, lines 134--163, reports plug-in estimation and bias-corrected semiparametric root-\(n\) inference with asymptotic normality for causal \(k\)-means targets.
Section 3.1, Theorem 3.1 and Section 3.2, Proposition 3.1 on PDF pages 10--12 give a margin-dependent fixed-resolution excess-distortion upper bound and a fixed-\(k\) minimax lower bound.

The title page and Abstract on page 3643 state simultaneous confidence regions for many functional parameters using approximately Neyman-orthogonal scores and high-dimensional uniform central limit theory.
Preprint Theorem 2.1 gives Gaussian approximation for hyperrectangles, and Section 4 gives multiplier-bootstrap approximation for maxima of supplied high-dimensional sums.
The manuscript sharpens Gaussian and bootstrap approximation rates for nondegenerate high-dimensional covariance structures.
The article derives lower bounds for the length of honest adaptive nonparametric confidence intervals.
The paper studies plug-in hierarchical linkages and density level sets of vector counterfactual features.

Abstract p. 1 and Introduction pp. 3–4 study convergence of optimal K-level quantizers and distortion performance for Wasserstein-convergent probability-measure sequences, including empirical measures, with bounds depending on the quantization level.

tldr: Adjacent causal-clustering resolutions share reoptimized codebooks and highly structured noise, so their joint inferential price is determined by the covariance geometry of their efficient scores rather than by the number of reported resolutions alone. The proposal computes the full uniform-law covariance through periodic Bernoulli polynomials and greatest-common-divisor identities, proves that the resulting process contains a linearly growing separated packing, derives a corrected cross-fitted band with intrinsic Gaussian-width radius, and matches it over the explicit local experiment \(\mathcal U_n\) with a genuine multi-resolution Fano lower bound whose tilted observed-data laws remain in one nondegenerate quantizer neighborhood.

project_justification.gap: Fixed-resolution causal \(k\)-means inference and quantizer geometry do not determine the covariance-aware minimax price of reporting an entire adjacent causal-distortion process. LiuPages2020 overlaps the optimizer- and distortion-performance-stability ingredient at fixed or level-by-level quantization, but its verified scope does not provide uniform \(K\le K_n\) control at shrinking adjacent-score scales, causal nuisance correction, joint adjacent efficient-score covariance, multiplier calibration, or a multi-resolution causal Fano lower bound. High-dimensional bootstrap theory treats supplied score arrays rather than this optimized causal process.
project_justification.niche: The exact cross-resolution kernel creates a theorem-level route to distinguish an intrinsic joint penalty from a crude coordinate-count penalty and to certify that penalty by a causal observed-data packing.
project_justification.fill: The project derives the arithmetic covariance and semimetric, controls optimized-risk and nuisance remainders at the associated Gaussian width, and proves matching upper and Fano lower bounds over the explicit local experiment \(\mathcal U_n\), while retaining only uniform linearization over the broader causal-quantizer class.

related_work: The published Abstract of KimKimKennedy2026, lines 134--163, is the verified source for plug-in estimation and bias-corrected semiparametric root-\(n\) inference with asymptotic normality for causal \(k\)-means; it is used here only for fixed-resolution influence-function ingredients. Pollard1982Central supplies fixed-\(k\) center asymptotics. Levrard2015, Section 3.1, Theorem 3.1 and Section 3.2, Proposition 3.1 on PDF pages 10--12, supplies margin-dependent fixed-resolution excess-distortion bounds and a fixed-\(k\) minimax lower bound. LiuPages2020, Abstract page 1 and Introduction pages 3--4, studies convergence of optimal \(K\)-level quantizers and distortion performance for Wasserstein-convergent probability-measure sequences, including empirical measures, with quantization-level-dependent bounds; it is a fixed- and level-by-level antecedent for the optimizer/performance-stability ingredient, not a comparator with the joint frontier. Its verified scope does not provide uniform \(K\le K_n\) control at shrinking adjacent-score scales, causal nuisance correction, joint adjacent efficient-score covariance, multiplier calibration, or a multi-resolution causal Fano lower bound.
